title: Discrete random spacetimes: covariance and quantization in growth dynamics for causal sets
version: PhD thesis, Imperial College London, 2021; publisher/deposit PDF 'Zalel-S-2021-PhD-Thesis.pdf', 2,195,161 bytes, sha256 8ee86f76f5a033f9ff71941d511e4267f1cb28441aa76f3aa7391f74b847c86f; read from Imperial Spiral on 2026-10-20. Chapter 6 (pp.89-91 in the PDF's printed pagination) was read in full; other chapters were searched for 'doubly', 'complex percolation', 'valency', 'post' and 'future work'.
section_locator: Ch.6, pp.89-91: 'Complex Transitive Percolation' on reduced poscau and on 'super-reduced poscau' (the 2023 paper's doubly-reduced poscau); p.90 states that every level n>1 contains valency-one nodes, that the earlier criterion cannot decide bounded variation, and that the valency-one term 'could be computed using techniques similar to those used to obtain the probability of a post in section 6.1. We leave this calculation for future work.' Fig.6.3a,b.
relevance: The closest prior source for the selected open case: it defines super-reduced poscau, states the valency-one obstruction, sketches the amended inequality, and explicitly leaves the decisive computation open. It does not prove the doubly-principal classification.
assumptions: Complex Transitive Percolation amplitudes A_p(C)=p^L(1-p)^{binom(n,2)-R}; complex Markovian dynamics on reduced/super-reduced poscau; finite-valency tree with no maximal elements; extension criterion via zeta and S_n; valency-one nodes excluded from the minimum-zeta criterion and handled by an amended S_n bound.
conclusion: Author's claim: on reduced poscau the numerical minima suggest zeta_n^min=|p|+|1-p|-1 for n=2,3,4; on super-reduced poscau the amended criterion leaves the valency-one term unresolved, so no classification is established. The thesis suggests, but does not prove, nonextension for p not in [0,1].
proof_status: Numerical n=2,3,4 evidence plus an amended inequality sketch; no all-level proof of the valency-one term; explicitly 'left for future work'. This is the open case closed by research/creative/RESULT.md.
open_questions: Whether the valency-one sum diverges for all p outside [0,1]; the thesis leaves this open. The 2023 paper repeats the same open question. No later source found in the bounded search.
limits: Thesis PDF, not the 2023 published paper; page numbers are the PDF's printed pages. Searches of other chapters were keyword-based. Not a priority certificate.
